findings.title: canManage() grants manage on VIEW permission
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() calls hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). An admin who holds only the 'view' scope on all groups is therefore treated as able to manage groups, for example creating top-level groups via addTopLevelGroup. This is a privilege escalation. The check should require only the MANAGE scope.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource IDs, not group IDs
findings.body: In V2, group resources are named by the group ID, but the code passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission (which looks the resource up by name) and adds groupResource.getId() to the result set. The returned set therefore holds authz resource IDs instead of group IDs. The users search and count group filters will match nothing, or fall back to the all-groups resource. Use groupResource.getName() in both places.

findings.title: Possible NPE when all-groups resource is missing
findings.body: getResourceTypeResource can return null, for example when the schema is unsupported or the 'Groups' resource is absent. hasPermission then passes that null to policyStore.findByResource and later calls resource.getScopes(), which throws a NullPointerException. A null check is needed before using the resource.

findings.title: Permission results not filtered by resource ID
findings.body: Unlike UserPermissionsV2, this loop accepts a matching scope from any permission returned by the evaluation, without checking permission.getResourceId() against the evaluated resource. Scopes granted on other resources could therefore satisfy the check for this group. Filter the permissions by resource ID, as UserPermissionsV2 does.

findings.title: Group permission scan now runs on every user search
findings.body: searchForUser now always calls getGroupIdsWithViewPermission. That method calls users().canView(), which can itself trigger a policy evaluation, and it then evaluates permissions for every group resource. Previously this work was skipped when users().canView() was already true. The cost is duplicated or extra evaluation on every user search.
